deep.reconstruction:
The page is a summary table, probably closing a file. It sorts the smallest arrangements of n lines (or pseudolines) in the real projective plane P^2(R) by combinatorial type. For each type it records two things.

(i) Rigidity. 'Standard projectif' means all realizations of the type are projectively equivalent, so the realization space is one PGL3(R)-orbit. 'Standard combinatoire' means all arrangements in that position (for example general position) have the same combinatorial type.

(ii) Three symmetry groups and whether they agree:
- 'autom proj / comp. neutre': pi_0 of the stabilizer of the arrangement in PGL3(R), i.e. projective automorphisms modulo the identity component;
- 'autom comb': automorphisms of the induced cell decomposition of P^2;
- 'aut. cont': homeomorphisms preserving the arrangement, up to isotopy.

The entries, checked one by one:

n=1: standard.

n=2: standard. The cell complex has 1 vertex, 2 loop edges and 2 bigons. Projectively, with lines x=0 and y=0, the stabilizer is diag(a,b,1) together with the swap; pi_0 is (Z/2)^2 extended by the swap, which is D4 of order 8. The vertex link is an 8-gon-like circle with 4 marked points and the antipodal identification; its symmetry group is again D4. So the line plausibly ends '≃ aut. carré' (the group of the square).

n=3, general position: the complex is the hemi-octahedron (3 vertices, 6 edges, 4 triangles). The stabilizer of a triangle is the torus extended by S3, with pi_0 = (Z/2)^2 ⋊ S3 = S4. This equals the octahedral group modulo ±1, which is the rotation group of the cube. So the entry should read '≃ aut. cube orienté'.

n=3, concurrent: the complex has 1 vertex, 3 loops and 3 discs. Combinatorial automorphisms are the symmetries of the vertex link, a circle with 6 points carrying the antipodal involution: the dihedral group of order 12, 'groupe de l'hexagone'. Projectively, normalize to matrices [[A,0],[c,1]] with A in R*·D3 inside GL2. Then pi_0 = Z/2 × S3, which is again order 12, isomorphic to D6. It is an extension involving Z/2 and Z/6 or S3, as written.

n=4, general position: projectively standard, since this is the dual of a projective frame. Every permutation of the lines is realized by a unique projective map, so Aut_proj = S4 = Aut_comb.

n=4, three concurrent: standard. Send the 4th line to infinity; then Aut = GL2-maps preserving 3 lines through the origin, with pi_0 = Z/2 × S3 ≅ D6, the hexagon group again.

n=4, four concurrent: not projectively standard because of the cross-ratio, but combinatorially standard. Aut_comb is the symmetry group of the link (8 points, antipodal), the dihedral group of order 16, 'groupe de l'octogone'. Grothendieck left Aut_proj blank. In fact pi_0(Aut_proj) depends on the realization:
- for a generic cross-ratio it is Z/2 × V4, of order 8;
- for the harmonic pencil (lines at 0°, 45°, 90°, 135°) the rotation by 45° gives an element of order 8 in pi_0, and pi_0 ≅ D8 = Aut_comb.

n=5, general position: not projectively standard (2-dimensional moduli), but combinatorially standard: there is a unique simple arrangement of 5 (pseudo)lines. It has 10 vertices, 20 edges and 11 faces (5 triangles, 5 quadrilaterals, 1 pentagon). The unique pentagon is fixed by every automorphism, so Aut_comb is D5, the 'groupe du pentagone'. It is realized by the regular pentagon arrangement.

n≥6, general position: not combinatorially standard; there are 4 simple types for n=6.

Purpose: this is a base-case census for Grothendieck's programme on systems of pseudolines. It tests whether combinatorial automorphisms are the same as topological ones (the mapping class group of the pair), and whether they come from pi_0 of projective symmetries. Rigidity holds up to n=4 (or 5 combinatorially), and coincidence of the groups holds at the maximally symmetric realizations.
errors: No real errors; the '(?)' after 'hexagone' and 'octogone' can be removed, since both are correct (orders 12 and 16).

For 4 concurrent lines the projective group was left blank. It is not constant over the realization space: generically pi_0 has order 8 (Z/2×V4). Only the harmonic pencil realizes the full octagon group D8.
For 4 lines in general position, the bracketed '≃ id' is ambiguous. The correct statement is Aut_proj ≅ Aut_comb ≅ S4, the stabilizer being finite.

ideas.what: Projective rigidity ('standard') of small line configurations: 1–4 lines, the 4-line types with 3 concurrent, and 3 concurrent lines are single PGL3-orbits; 4 concurrent and 5 general lines have moduli.
ideas.modern_name: realization spaces of line arrangements / oriented matroids
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (projective frames); realization spaces studied by Grünbaum, Ringel, Mnëv (1988)

ideas.what: Uniqueness of the simple arrangement for n≤5, and non-uniqueness for n=6 (four simple types).

Comparison of three symmetry groups: pi_0 of the projective stabilizer, combinatorial automorphisms of the cell complex, and the mapping class group of (P^2, arrangement). Identified explicitly as the square group (n=2), cube rotations/S4 (3 general), hexagon group (3 concurrent), octagon group (4 concurrent), pentagon group (5 general).
ideas.modern_name: automorphism groups of arrangements / symmetric realizations of oriented matroids
ideas.usually_credited_to: scattered: Grünbaum; Bokowski–Sturmfels; Ringel isotopy theorem

ideas.what: For n concurrent lines, the combinatorial automorphism group is the dihedral group of the 2n-gon (vertex link with antipodal involution).

missed.claim: The question left blank, whether the combinatorial automorphism group is always realized as pi_0 of the projective stabilizer of some maximally symmetric realization, is a real question. Here it holds: the harmonic pencil gives D8 and the regular pentagon gives D5. In general it fails, since some combinatorial symmetries of arrangements are not realizable by any symmetric stretching. That is known in the oriented-matroid literature, but not connected to Grothendieck.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only as historical evidence that Grothendieck framed pseudoline theory as a comparison between continuous, combinatorial and algebraic symmetry. This parallels his anabelian/dessins view (topological versus algebraic automorphisms). Mathematically it is known.

deep.surprise_reason: A correct, routine census of small arrangements and their symmetry groups. Its interest is only historical: it shows the three-way comparison projective/combinatorial/topological that organizes the pseudoline notes. No new results.
